name: Shaphan
title: King's Scribe
summary: Shaphan was a scribe (secretary) under King Josiah of Judah. He played a central role when the Book of the Law was found in the temple, and he read it aloud to the king. His descendants were also prominent officials who protected the prophet Jeremiah.

keyEvents.title: Shaphan Sent to the Temple
keyEvents.description: King Josiah sent Shaphan to the high priest Hilkiah to arrange for the repair of the temple.

keyEvents.title: The Book of the Law Is Found
keyEvents.description: Hilkiah found the Book of the Law in the house of the Lord and gave it to Shaphan, who read it.

keyEvents.title: Shaphan Reads the Book of the Law to the King
keyEvents.description: Shaphan read the Book of the Law aloud to King Josiah, which caused the king to tear his clothes in grief over the people's disobedience.

keyEvents.title: Shaphan Sent to the Prophetess Huldah
keyEvents.description: Josiah sent Shaphan and other officials to the prophetess Huldah to seek the word of the Lord concerning the Book of the Law that had been found.

keyEvents.title: Shaphan's Son Ahikam Protects Jeremiah
keyEvents.description: Ahikam, son of Shaphan, protected the prophet Jeremiah from those who wanted to kill him after his speech in the temple.

keyEvents.title: Shaphan's Descendants as Prominent Officials
keyEvents.description: Several of Shaphan's sons and grandsons served as officials. Gedaliah, son of Ahikam, son of Shaphan, was appointed governor over Judah after the fall of Jerusalem.
